description: Shipping notice from a shop: SPF, DKIM and DMARC pass, links stay on the sender's own domain.
Lookalike domain (paypa1), DMARC fail, Reply-To elsewhere, a button that shows paypal.com but points to the lookalike, tracking pixel, 24-hour threat.
Display name says Microsoft 365 but the address is a free-mail account. Authentication passes, so only the content and identity checks catch it.
Macro-enabled .docm attachment with an "Enable Content" lure, DKIM and DMARC fail. The attachment bytes are a harmless text placeholder.
CEO impersonation from free mail asking for gift cards, Reply-To on another domain, secrecy. Authentication passes and there are no links, so the evidence is all in the wording.
A user's "Forward as attachment" of the PayPal lookalike. The outer email is clean; the verdict must come from the embedded original.
A plain inline forward of the Microsoft lure. The original headers are gone, so sender checks are limited, but the quoted sender and the link are enough.
